Noisy Pixel
Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered brings the classic kaiju brawler roaring back with impressive rebuilt visuals, satisfying arena destruction, and chaotic multiplayer battles. While its limited roster and tedious character unlocks feel dated, the accessible combat and faithful Godzilla presentation make this a thoroughly entertaining return for the King of the Monsters.

Uagna.it
A respectful, carefully crafted remaster that brings a 2002 cult classic back to life with revamped visuals, larger destructible cities, and online multiplayer, while also retaining the original’s limitations in depth and roster variety. It’s a comeback that will delight longtime fans and anyone looking for evenings of good old destruction with friends, though it will satisfy less those expecting a modern, nuanced fighting game.

COGconnected
Right now, Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered is a great version of a good retro game. Because the game was remade from the ground up, I wish the developers had made a super version of the Godzilla trilogy with more content. While Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered’s combat is really fun, there’s not much depth. There are lots of modes, and a bit of RPG unlocking, but this isn’t a deep fighting game that’s going to be played at tournaments. It’s a great budget buy for Godzilla fans. But more content would have made Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered a more obvious recommendation. If you’re at all curious, or have any fondness for the original game, it remains a fun time.
PlayStation 5 FULL REVIEW
Nov 2, 2026
65
Multiplayer.it
In the media shadow of sacred monsters like Grand Theft Auto VI and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake, only an equally fearless monstrosity could face them: Godzilla. Nearly a quarter century after its release on GameCube, Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee returns with a remaster that discreetly refreshes the audiovisual experience and improves the progression without betraying its structure. The core is that of a 3D fighting game in which kaiju clashes are accompanied by the destruction of entire cities, in a blaze of explosions and particle effects. Behind this chaos lies a combat system that's immediate, but not always precise and balanced, suspended somewhere between classic fighting games and the festive jumble of a party game. The mechanics are simple, despite a certain unwieldiness in the movements, and the best of the action is found especially in local multiplayer. Boasting a competitive price and a structure with few pretensions, the title from Pipeworks Studios is mainly dedicated to fans of the Japanese monster and to those looking for a carefree interlude before throwing themselves into productions of a much higher calibre.
PlayStation 5 FULL REVIEW
